content.text:
This contradicts a design-system constraint, so I'm raising it instead of implementing it.

The guardrail **"The DS owns no data, fetching, timers or control; state arrives as props"** (from `$dooph-ds-writing-components`) prohibits a DS component from owning the fetch call or the 30-second polling timer. A `ServiceStatus` that accepts a URL and polls it internally would violate that rule.

**What the DS can own:** a presentational `ServiceStatusBadge` (or similar) that receives `status: "operational" | "degraded" | "down"` as a prop and renders the coloured Sticker + label. No URL, no `fetch`, no `setInterval`.

**What the consuming app owns:** the polling logic — calling the endpoint every 30 seconds and passing the current status down as a prop.

Want me to build the presentational version (prop-driven, no fetching), or do you want to remove the constraint first?
